items.title: Template Redo ignores later zoning and repurchases orphaned furniture after Load
items.body:
Completed template Redo ignores a genuine later zoning collision.

Checkpoint 4b5e06b4d279260318d34a7dd604bd46c6e9435f, actual packed kernel and current V8 encode/decode/restore; no browser or synthetic state.

Reproduce: complete mirrored 90° Basic Cell 10,10 → actual Undo → accepted ZoneRoom(room.yard,10,10,8,8) → live or encoded Load → Redo. The genuine Yard exists, and zoning did not clear construction Redo history.

Actual worker full-template preflight BEFORE Redo is false/structure-occupied at 10,10, with captured state unchanged. Redo nevertheless reapproves all 20 old orders, moves history and after real settlement charges 1530 again (23470→21940). Zoning overlap cancels 18 shell orders, but 2 completed source-owned Bed/Toilet objects remain inside Yard with no template ledger. The independently zoned Yard remains. This is a real second purchase/orphaned fixture outcome, not only history mutation.

Final baseline 2 RED /2 legal GREEN,503ms: both live and encoded Load collide; genuine no-later-zoning controls finish the complete Cell. Existing tests after later PlaceObject clear redoStack and cannot exercise this conflict. Initial closed StorageRoom3×3 probe had an invalid zoning precondition; corrected baseline uses accepted open Yard8×8.

Fresh duplicate check/full related bodies: #1687 restores pending obligation on legal unfinished Redo, already present here; #1657 accepted entire reversible template, not this new Redo admission conflict; #1985 is lost latest-action eligibility on Undo, different persisted state. No overlapping-zoning Redo report found.

[Published original/pre/immediate/settled captures and executable packed baseline](https://github.com/woogitsu/lockstate/blob/codex/template-redo-zoning-audit-20261003/docs/research/2026-10-03-template-redo-zoning/README.md).

Narrow granted fix scope: exact existing undone descriptors tied to actual current top Redo history, existing immutable full-footprint preflight before any order/history/spend mutation, existing build.unbuildable/build.unowned-land copy and actual tile. Coordinator/session-command only. Ordinary Redo, legal live/Load template controls and exact existing tariffs/schema stay unchanged. No format field or policy invented. Production negative/restore pending implementation checkpoint.

items.title: Canceling a JIT material delivery demolishes an occupied partially furnished room template
items.body:
## Reproduction

On published `9dc2abd1205ad9d6ce19f12187396e028b4c58b2`, packed commands and real scheduled construction reproduce this both live and after encoded V8 Save/Load:

- Purchase 648 bricks (funds 25000→−920), await delivery.
- Place mirrored 90° `cell-row-four` at (10,10). Complete actual shell and first Bed;3 Beds still materials-pending, funds −1245.
- Admit a prisoner; wait actual room occupancy 1.
- Sell 3 bricks for 60. The scheduler buys1 wood plank for 65, funds −1250, pending delivery `jit:3730:item.wood-plank:0`.
- At tick 3731, `CancelMaterialPurchase` that delivery.

Actual: funds −1250→−1185, all 66 template orders canceled, physical Bed/walls/doors removed, but one occupied room remains registered without its shell/bed. The same result after V8 Load.

Expected under existing #1657/#1608 atomic occupied-template reversal: existing `unzone.room-occupied` refusal before procurement refund or order/world/history mutation. This asks for no new copy/schema/tariff/policy.

## Boundary and controls

The same genuine partial construction without a resident legally cancels all 66 orders and refunds 65; encodedLoad plus 150 ticks does not rebuy. Permanent packed regression:2 RED / 2 legal GREEN, 3.02 s, `tests/integration/room-template-occupied-material-cancel.test.ts`.

Existing all 160 rotation/mirror completion/Load/UndoRedo matrix is green, and existing template economy tests cancel delivery before occupancy. The missed state is zoned, partially furnished, occupied, with a later real JIT purchase. Fresh searches for CancelMaterialPurchase and occupied delivery plus full #1657/#687 bodies found no issue covering this entry point. Related #687 fixes automatic repurchase and must remain intact.

## Source cause

`runtime/session-commands.ts` calls `procurement.cancel` before `construction.withdrawOrdersAwaitingMaterial` and `roomTemplates.reconcileCancelledShells`. It omits the existing coupled reversal preparation; reconciliation ignores failed individual unzone before removing shell/fixtures.

Proposed narrow scope: pure predicted withdrawal IDs in ConstructionSystem; collective exact template membership/unzone preparation in Coordinator; supply command preflight before refund. No source edit yet.

Earlier wrong overdraft/setup probes are recorded as fixture errors, not production failures. No browser/CI polling.

Published diagnostic: a2b057d42d79059d7a72a8fe40cea83d297483e2 on codex/noncell-template-playability-audit-20261003.

items.title: Refused occupied template cancellation blocks Undo of a newer independent purchase
items.body:
# Refused template cancellation changes Undo selection eligibility

Read-only packed runtime diagnosis on published `39448e8956da264c1833a71cf9d4bb6faa30a689`, 2026-10-03. No production edit in this checkpoint.

## Actual reproduction

1. Purchase 648 bricks, await real delivery, then place mirrored 90° `cell-row-four` at (10,10).
2. Actual scheduled construction completes its shell and first bed, with three beds still materials-pending. Admit a real resident and await occupancy one.
3. Place and complete an independent ordinary full-square wall at (2,2). This is the newest accepted construction gesture. Funds stay −1,245 because its two bricks come from genuine purchased stock. The original physical bed retains its exact template source-order owner.
4. Continue live, or encode/decode/restore V8 NOW, before the next press.
5. Cancel the original completed template bed by actual current order revision. Existing occupied-room protection correctly refuses `unzone.room-occupied`; the captured gameplay snapshot is unchanged except kernel bookkeeping.
6. Immediately Undo. Expected: reverse the newer independent wall, retain the occupied template and its owners. Actual: the wall remains completed; the attempted cancellation set the hidden newer-action flag before its refusal, so Undo refuses.

Targeted baseline **2 RED / 2 legal GREEN**, 4.91 s. Both no-refusal controls, live and saved, correctly Undo only the independent wall. No fake world, treasury, history, owner or resident state was injected. The encoded Load is BEFORE the refused cancellation, so this is not #1985's loss of a previously accepted newer-action marker after Load.

## Existing accepted rule and deduplication

ADR0104's accepted option 2 uses the newest accepted command. Its 2026-09-23 amendment explains that this means the newest command which changed something; refused placement leaves eligibility as it was. Existing source comment on `noteActionThatDoesNotWriteTheUndoStack` also says accepted commands. This cancellation changes no prison or transaction and has already reported its refusal.

Full fresh bodies #1657, #1986, #1990, #1975, #956 and #1985 were read. Refused/Undo issue search found no matching cancellation report. #1657 protects the coupled reversal, #1990 preserves selection across deferred construction, #1986 guards conflicting Redo, #1975 protects physical ownership, and #1985 is the separately reserved persistent marker. None requires a new schema or policy here.

Cause: `SessionCommands` marks every non-construction command before the existing template cancellation preflight. Intended narrow scope: execute the existing coupled current-revision preflight before the generic accepted-action marker; successful non-Undo construction cancellation keeps its existing marker. Source lease, production negative, restoration and wider gates are pending. No browser was launched.

items.title: Ordinary Build accepts an object footprint through a completed full-square wall
items.body:
## Reproduction
On the current full-square/template stack, complete a Basic Cell at (10,10). In Build, order a 1×2 wooden bed anchored at (12,15). Its anchor is clear, but the second tile (12,16) is the cell's completed south wall (`squareStructure=1`). The order is accepted and materials can be reserved despite intersecting the wall. Reproduced in the real 1920×1080 browser worker flow and a direct simulation test.

## Expected
Object placement checks the entire footprint against completed full-square structures, refuses `place-object.tile-occupied` before queuing or cost, and keeps the room intact across Save/Load. Existing placed-object and pending-order footprint checks already iterate these tiles; square structures need the same check.

Related: #1586, #1639. #1639 covers furniture emitted *by* a ready room plan; this covers ordinary Build `PlaceObject` after the room is complete.

items.title: [Docs] The twelve `20260824` migrations are recorded as unapplied to hosted staging, while the accepted delivery mechanism says every merge to `main` applies them — 165 commits have landed since
items.body:
Two Accepted, load-bearing statements about the hosted staging database cannot both be true, and the repository currently asserts both.

* **`docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md:92-114` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:224`** state that the twelve migrations dated `20260824` are **not** applied to the hosted staging project, and enumerate what staging therefore still carries.
* **ADR 0016 §1 (Accepted) and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:145,161`** state that merging to `main` applies whatever is pending, automatically, through Supabase's own GitHub integration, and that the trigger is the merge rather than the diff.

All twelve are on `origin/main`. **165 commits — roughly thirty merges — have landed on `main` since the last of them.** Under the mechanism the repository says is live, they were applied on the first of those merges, on 2026-08-24.

This matters more than an ordinary stale sentence: `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:224` is the paragraph an operator reads to decide what a hosted database contains before touching it, and it is a list of security controls it says are absent.

## The two claims, quoted

`docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md:92-98`:

```
- **Not applied anywhere but a scratch database:** the twelve migrations
  dated `20260824` — everything from
  `20260824090000_pin_trigger_function_search_path.sql` through
  `20260824150000_revoke_trusted_truncate.sql`. They are all
  newer than the hosted apply above, so the hosted project still carries the
  declarations, grants, constraints and function bodies as they stood on
  2026-08-23 until they are pushed.
```

and again at `:109-114`, about `20260824150000` specifically: *"a single `REVOKE`, applied to a scratch database only, so whatever `TRUNCATE` the hosted project grants `service_role` is untouched until it is pushed"*.

`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:224`:

> The **twelve** added since — every migration dated `20260824` … — are **not** applied there yet, so the hosted project still carries the pre-#105 function declarations, the ambient client `TRUNCATE` for both the client roles and `service_role`, the caller-asserted challenge-evidence dedup key, the webhook-only ledger idempotency key, an unvalidated `save_versions.storage_path`, unbounded text, `jsonb` and scalar columns on both tiers, and the table-level INSERT grants that let a client stamp its own `created_at`.

Against `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:145`:

| Migrations → Supabase **staging** | automatically, on every merge to `main`, through Supabase's own GitHub integration | none |

and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:161`, which forecloses the obvious escape:

> **Read that row as "on every merge", not "when migration files change".** PR #87 touched `deploy.yml`, this document and an ADR — no file under `supabase/migrations/` — and the migrations were applied anyway. The integration applies whatever is *pending* on a push to the configured branch. A pull request that changes nothing about the schema still triggers the apply; a merge is the trigger, not the diff.

and ADR 0016 §1, whose Status is **Accepted**:

> The Supabase GitHub integration is connected to `matmaxalez/lockstate` with **Deploy to production** enabled, pointed at the `lockstate` project. Merging to `main` applies migrations to it without further approval.

## Measured

From this checkout, against `origin/main`:

```
$ git ls-tree --name-only origin/main supabase/migrations/ | grep 20260824 | wc -l
12

$ git log --format="%h %ad %s" --date=short -1 origin/main -- supabase/migrations/20260824090000_pin_trigger_function_search_path.sql
7ed806a 2026-08-24 Key challenge-evidence dedup on the payload, not the caller's claim (#105)

$ git log --format="%h %ad %s" --date=iso origin/main -- supabase/migrations/20260824150000_revoke_trusted_truncate.sql
b867a4e 2026-08-24 13:07:53 +0000 Revoke TRUNCATE on public from service_role (#163)

$ git rev-list --count b867a4e..origin/main
165

$ git log --oneline -1 origin/main
5044f59 chore(release): v0.0.76
```

The merges since include `#320`…`#336` and every `chore(release)` between v0.0.62 and v0.0.76, spanning 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-26.

Also measured, because ADR 0016's Consequences section predicted it and it is still true:

```
$ grep -c "integration\|db push" docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md
0
```

## Which claim is false

Exactly one of these holds, and this repository cannot tell which from inside itself:

1. **The integration is applying on merge, as ADR 0016 §1 says.** Then hosted staging has carried all twelve since 2026-08-24, and both documents are false — including a list of eight named security controls `DEPLOYMENT.md:224` says are missing there and which are in fact present. The one genuinely useful sentence in that paragraph, that two of the twelve *can refuse to apply* on a populated project, would then describe an event that already resolved one way or the other, unrecorded.
2. **The integration is not applying on merge.** Then ADR 0016 §1 is false, `DEPLOYMENT.md:145` and `:161` are false, and the arrangement the owner accepted retroactively is not the arrangement that is running. ADR 0016 §2's constraint — production is a separate project and the integration is never repointed at it — rests on §1 being an accurate description of a live configuration, so a false §1 makes §2 a guard on something nobody has confirmed exists.

Either branch is worth knowing. The current state is worse than either, because the two are cited by each other: `CLOUD_SAVE.md:86-88` sources its hosted-state claim to `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, "Database migrations", and that section's own "Automated deployment" cross-reference (`:224`, last sentence: *"What applied them is covered under 'Automated deployment'"*) points at the table that contradicts it.

## Property violated

- `CLAUDE.md`: "Use repository docs and ADRs as the source of truth." Two sources of truth disagree about the same database.
- ADR 0016's Consequences names this document by name and marks the obligation open: *"`docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md` still needs the same amendment, and this consequence is **not** discharged."* That entry frames the gap as CLOUD_SAVE.md failing to *mention* the mechanism. The measurement above shows it is worse than an omission: the fact it records is inconsistent with the mechanism, not merely silent about it.
- ADR 0016's Context makes the stakes explicit: *"Reviewing a pull request that touches `supabase/migrations/` is now reviewing a deployment."* A reviewer who believes `CLOUD_SAVE.md:92` reviews it as scratch-database SQL.

## Failure scenario

An operator preparing to push migrations reads `DEPLOYMENT.md:224`, sees the twelve listed as unapplied, and runs `migrate-database.yml` against staging with `dry_run` unchecked to apply them. If branch 1 is what is true, `supabase db push` skips them — ADR 0016 §3 says so and that path is idempotent, so nothing breaks and the belief survives unchallenged. The same operator then reasons about the *production* project from the same paragraph. That is where a wrong belief about which controls are live stops being free: the eight controls `:224` lists as absent include the revoked `service_role` TRUNCATE on the append-only ledger (#163) and the table-level INSERT grant that lets a client stamp `created_at` (#194), and planning a production cutover around their absence produces a different plan from planning around their presence.

The reverse case is worse. If branch 2 is true, every future merge that touches `supabase/migrations/` is reviewed as a deployment, gets the extra scrutiny ADR 0016 asks for — and then nothing deploys, so a schema change believed live is not, and the first thing to notice is a client failing against a database that is a dozen migrations behind.

## Smallest fix

One observation settles it, and it is the observation both documents already say is outstanding: a `dry_run` of `migrate-database.yml` against `staging` (`target: staging`, `dry_run` left at its default `true`) prints `supabase migration list` for the live project. That is read-only by construction — ADR 0016 §3 calls it *"the only way to *inspect* the divergence between repository and project without changing anything"* — and it names, per timestamp, which of the twelve are remote.

Then, whichever way it comes back:

- Correct the false half. If applied: `CLOUD_SAVE.md:92-114` and `DEPLOYMENT.md:224` become a record of what staging carries, with the applied-on date and the mechanism, and the two constraints that could have refused get their outcome recorded. If not applied: ADR 0016 §1 gets a Status correction, because it describes a configuration that is not doing what it says.
- Discharge ADR 0016's open consequence in the same change, by naming the mechanism in `docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md` — the word "integration" appears zero times in it today — so a reader of that file alone learns that a merge applies migrations.
- Stop the pair from drifting again. Both documents state a hosted fact with a date and no way to check it. The cheapest durable form is to record the observation each time with the run id of the dry run that produced it, the way `DEPLOYMENT.md:159` already does for the 2026-08-23 window, rather than as a bare assertion.

No code, no migration, no schema change. Nothing under `supabase/migrations/` should be touched to resolve this.

## What would change my mind

- A `supabase migration list` output, or an equivalent read of the hosted project, showing the twelve as local-only. That would make branch 2 true and move the whole finding onto ADR 0016. **This was deliberately not attempted here** — nothing in this review was pointed at a hosted project — so the hosted state is genuinely UNKNOWN from where this was written, and that is the point: the repository asserts it twice, in two incompatible ways, and neither assertion is backed by an observation newer than 2026-08-23.
- Evidence that the Supabase integration was disconnected or its production branch changed after 2026-08-24. That lives in a dashboard outside this repository — ADR 0016 §2 says so explicitly (*"a two-click change in a dashboard, with no code review and no trace in this repository"*) — so nothing here could rule it out, and if it happened, ADR 0016 §1 is the document that has to say so.
- A reading of `DEPLOYMENT.md:145` under which a merge that does not touch `supabase/migrations/` does not apply pending migrations. `:161` exists specifically to refuse that reading, and cites PR #87 as the case that settled it.

items.title: [Operations] Implement jobs, logistics, inventories and utility capacity foundation
items.body:
## Resolution

Implemented in `src/simulation/operations/` (commit 2da9cb3, branch `claude/lockstate-continuation-rg2xbw`): a deterministic carry-job lifecycle, a transactional `Container` inventory model, and a capacity-graph `UtilityNetwork` for electricity/water — built on top of #14 (entity storage), #16 (construction), #21/#22 (navigation) and #23 (item catalog) rather than parallel implementations. Full design writeup: `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **Eligible workers deterministically claim and execute jobs.** `JobSystem.assignAvailableJobs` matches highest-priority-first, then ascending id, to the first idle worker able to reserve the job's stock — `tests/unit/operations-job-system.test.ts`.
- [x] **Cancellation/failure releases reservations consistently.** `failJob`/`cancel` both release the source reservation and free the worker; `cancel` specifically guards against releasing a reservation a still-`'available'` job never made (a real bug found and fixed — see below) — `tests/unit/operations-job-system.test.ts`.
- [x] **Items move only through validated inventory transfer/carry tasks.** `Container` has no direct stock-subtract method; every removal goes through `reserve`→`withdrawReserved`. Every `CarryItemJob` travels both legs through the real `NavigationSystem` — `tests/unit/operations-inventory.test.ts`.
- [x] **Representative delivery→storage→kitchen/canteen, laundry and waste flows work headlessly.** All three now demonstrated through the identical substrate (delivery/storage/kitchen concurrently with a construction order sharing the same `JobBoard`/`ContainerRegistry`; laundry with dirty→clean conversion; waste including a mid-flight cancellation) — `tests/unit/operations-representative-flows.test.ts`.
- [x] **Construction orders can wait for and consume delivered materials.** `ConstructionSystem` takes an optional `ConstructionMaterialsProvider` (default unlimited, #16 unchanged); `ContainerMaterialsProvider` checks all requirements before withdrawing any (all-or-nothing) — `tests/unit/operations-construction-integration.test.ts`.
- [x] **Electricity/water consumers respond to capacity/connectivity/failure state.** `UtilityNetwork` evaluates per connected component; three typed states (`powered`/`disabled-no-supply`/`disabled-failure`); both electricity and water networks tested, including disconnected components and un-failing a node — `tests/unit/operations-utility-network.test.ts`.
- [x] **Shortages, blocked routes and overloads are observable and typed.** `InventoryError` discriminated union (`insufficient-stock`/`insufficient-reserved`); `UtilityNodeState` typed states; route failures surface the navigation system's typed reason on `job.failReason`; a job with insufficient source stock stays `'available'` (observable backpressure) rather than erroring.
- [x] **Snapshot/restore preserves queues, reservations, inventories and networks.** `Container`, `ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool` (previously had none — added) and `UtilityNetwork` all round-trip together in one combined scenario against fresh `Kernel`/`NavigationSystem` instances, including a job interrupted mid-`'travelling'` — `tests/unit/operations-snapshot-restore.test.ts`.

## Test requirements coverage

- Assignment priority/eligibility/fairness — `operations-job-system.test.ts`.
- Inventory conservation and concurrent reservation — `operations-inventory.test.ts`.
- Route failure/cancellation recovery — `operations-job-system.test.ts` (permission-denied route failure; cancel-before-reservation).
- Representative operational flow integration — `operations-representative-flows.test.ts`.
- Utility graph/capacity/breakdown — `operations-utility-network.test.ts`.
- Deterministic replay and save/restore — `operations-snapshot-restore.test.ts`.

## Performance requirements

`tests/unit/operations-scale.test.ts`: 300 concurrent carry jobs across 20 workers on a 40-cell block run to completion with conserved inventory and zero leftover reservations (wall time logged as directional evidence only, per `docs/BENCHMARKING.md`'s no-hard-threshold policy); a 501-node utility network (1 producer, 500 consumers) evaluates correctly with deterministic ascending-id allocation. Assignment uses indexed idle-worker/available-job lists, not every-worker×every-job scans; utility evaluation is revision-cached, not a per-tick rescan.

## Real bugs found and fixed while building this

- `JobSystem` never actually started travel after assignment — jobs got stuck at `'assigned'` forever (missing `beginLeg` call).
- `JobSystem.cancel()` released a reservation unconditionally, which could silently steal a *different* job's real reservation for the same item (`Container` tracks reservations per item, not per job) when cancelling a job that was still `'available'`.
- `JobBoard.loadSnapshot` didn't handle a restored `'travelling'` job's stale `pathRequestId` (referencing the *previous* `NavigationSystem` instance's queue) — now drops such jobs back to `'assigned'` to re-request routing, matching `PrisonerOperationsRuntime`'s existing restore convention.
- `JobWorkerPool` had no snapshot/restore at all — worker busy-state would not have survived a save/restore boundary; added.

## Verification

```
pnpm typecheck   # clean
pnpm test        # 337/338 -- only the pre-existing, unrelated Node-version-pin
                  # failure (tests/foundation/repository-contract.test.ts,
                  # sandbox runs Node v22.22.2 vs. the repo's v24.19.0 pin)
pnpm build       # clean, bundle size unchanged (1,384.01 kB) -- this code
                  # is not wired into main.ts, no session UI exists yet,
                  # matching #19/#22/#24's precedent
```

## Out of scope (per the issue, and per `docs/OPERATIONS.md`)

Full economy pricing; final vehicle traffic/exports/farming/workshop production; detailed HVAC/CFD or electrical engineering simulation; advanced staff morale/skills; final UI/visual effects; a fully generic job-kind registry (one concrete job kind — `CarryItemJob` — plus reusable lifecycle/assignment machinery, per "representative flows prove extensibility").

items.title: [ADR] Four ADR statuses contradict the code, all in the same direction: Proposed decisions already shipped (plus the owner's approval queue)
items.body:
> **Corrected — 2026-08-24.** Re-verified against `main` at `9b6965a` (v0.0.16). **All four defects are still live** and are unchanged in substance; only their line references have moved, and those are corrected in place. What was false was the *framing* around them:
>
> - *"`docs/adr/` holds **17 ADRs**: twelve Accepted, five Proposed."* — **replaced.** There are **20 ADRs** plus the README. The split is **14 Accepted** (0001–0011, 0017, 0019, 0020) and **6 Proposed** (0012, 0013, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0021). Read from the files.
> - *"**Nothing in the repository lists what is awaiting approval**; it is recoverable only by grepping seventeen files for two different Status syntaxes."* — **deleted; false.** `docs/adr/README.md` is now exactly that index, and it says so in its own second sentence: *"the only recorded statement of which numbers are taken."* Its table carries every ADR's status verbatim. The **mechanical half this issue asked for also exists**: `tests/foundation/adr-numbering-contract.test.ts` parses both Status syntaxes against a closed keyword set, requires the row count to equal the number of ADR files, and fails when a row's status disagrees with the document it points at — so a status edit that does not update the index now breaks the suite.
> - *"Add **0018** … and **0019** … if those land — both are also authored `Proposed`."* — **deleted; false both ways.** 0019 landed **Accepted**, and 0018 will never land: PR #91 was closed as superseded and `docs/adr/README.md:44` now marks the number *"Free — released when PR #91 was closed as superseded"*.
>
> The rest of the issue stands as filed, including the pattern it names.

Verified against `origin/main` @ `06e187c`; re-verified at `9b6965a`. Statuses read from the files; every code claim re-checked.

## The pattern

`docs/adr/` holds **20 ADRs**: fourteen Accepted, six Proposed. Auditing each Status against the code found the control defect running in **one direction only** — no Accepted ADR was found unimplemented, but every Proposed ADR has already been implemented in whole or in part, and one Accepted ADR describes a state machine the code cannot occupy. The repository is deciding architecture in implementation and then leaving the ADR to ask for permission afterwards, which is precisely what `CLAUDE.md` forbids:

> If a necessary architectural decision is genuinely absent, create or propose an ADR instead of silently deciding inside implementation code.

Four located defects follow. Item 1 is a **code** fix; items 2–4 are prose fixes plus, for 0016, a decision only the owner can make.

---

## 1. ADR 0006's `ready` state is declared and never entered — the handshake gates nothing (Accepted ADR, false against code)

`docs/adr/0006-simulation-worker-adapter.md:14`
```
2. **ready**: Handshake completes. It awaits the `simulation/initialize` message containing initial game state/RNG seeds.
```

`src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts:27`
```ts
export type WorkerState =
  …
  | 'ready'
```

**VERIFIED, still true at `9b6965a`:** `'ready'` is a member of the `WorkerState` union and **no `transition()` call anywhere targets it**. All four transitions in the file go elsewhere — `:349` `'faulted'`, `:457` `'paused'`, `:492` `'paused'`/`'running'`, `:601` `'shutting-down'`. `git grep -n "'ready'" origin/main -- src tests` returns exactly one line: the union member at `:27`. It appears in no test.

Two consequences:
- ADR 0006's state 2 describes a state the machine cannot occupy.
- The handshake is **not a gate**. `handleHandshake` checks `if (this._state !== 'uninitialized')`, answers, and transitions nothing; `handleInitialize` also requires `'uninitialized'` and goes straight to `'paused'`. So a `simulation/initialize` sent as the very first message, with no handshake at all, **succeeds** and builds a live kernel.

That contradicts ADR 0006's own Consequences ("Enforces strict initialization protocol; main thread cannot send commands before the kernel is ready") and ADR 0003 decision 4 (a version-1 handshake advertises supported versions and capabilities *before* initialization).

**LIVE, but latent in impact.** Nothing breaks today because the only client does handshake first. It becomes a real defect the moment a second envelope version exists and capability negotiation matters: an implementation that skips the handshake works, ships, and then silently skips version negotiation.

**Smallest correct fix — in the code, because the ADR describes the safer machine:** add `this.transition('ready')` at the end of `handleHandshake`, and change `handleInitialize`'s guard from `!== 'uninitialized'` to `!== 'ready'`, faulting `'not-initialized'` otherwise. If the owner prefers the current behaviour, then delete `'ready'` from the union and rewrite ADR 0006 state 2 — but ADR 0003 decision 4 then needs the same amendment, so the cheap-looking option is the one that costs two ADR edits.

**Test that should have caught it:** `tests/unit/worker-state-machine.test.ts` asserts that a handshake is answered; nothing asserts what happens *without* one. **Surviving mutation:** delete the entire `handleHandshake` branch's state check, or send `simulation/initialize` first — the suite stays green either way. The test to add: "a `simulation/initialize` sent before any handshake is refused with a `not-initialized` fault", plus one asserting `state === 'ready'` after a handshake.

---

## 2. ADR 0012's identifier table is wrong on both axes for path-request ids, and its own escape clause has already fired (Proposed)

`docs/adr/0012-derived-identifier-reproducibility.md:27`
```
| path request ids | per-system `requestSequence` | no | no — but consumed only by a `NavigationSystem` that a restore rebuilds empty |
```

**Snapshotted? VERIFIED yes, still.** `src/persistence/save-schema.ts:402` (`carryItemJobSchema`) and `:451` (the prisoner action section) both carry:
```ts
    pathRequestId: z.string().min(1).optional(),
```
Both live inside `sessionSystemsV3Schema` (`:767-775`), which is the `simulation` field of the shipped V3 payload. `JobBoard.getSnapshot` writes jobs unfiltered, so any save taken while a job is `'travelling'` contains the id, and the envelope checksum covers it.

**Minted by? VERIFIED wrong.** `JobSystem` uses no `requestSequence`; it derives the id from state — `src/simulation/operations/job-system.ts`:
```ts
    const requestId = `job.${job.id}.${job.leg}.${tick}`;
```

**The escape clause has expired.** ADR 0012's own Consequences:
```
- Path-request ids stay category 2 by exception: they are consumed only within
  one `NavigationSystem` lifetime, which a restore rebuilds empty
  ([ADR 0007](./0007-navigation-work-budgets-and-flow-fields.md)). If routing
  state ever enters a save, they become category 1.
```
Routing state has entered the save. The restore side already knows — `src/simulation/operations/job.ts` deliberately discards the id and drops the job back to `'assigned'`.

**LIVE.** ADR 0012 is the taxonomy every future id-minting subsystem is told to follow, and ADR 0015 extends it. An agent reading the table believes category-2 ids never cross a save boundary and will feel free to snapshot others, or will skip the restore-side clearing that `loadSnapshot` had to add by hand.

**Smallest correct fix:** correct the two cells and replace the Consequences bullet with the fact that the trigger condition is met, then choose one of two remedies — strip `pathRequestId` in `JobBoard.getSnapshot` (smaller, and matches what `loadSnapshot` already assumes), or promote path-request ids to category 1 with a snapshotted counter. Stripping is an implementation choice; promoting changes the save format and needs the ADR to be accepted first.

Related: the same table's `GlobalTopologyId` row is the subject of #112, which is the one entry it already calls "actually wrong rather than merely undecided" — that half is being handled there and is not re-filed here.

---

## 3. ADR 0015's to-do list is complete, and its decision is already in the save format while its Status still asks whether it should be (Proposed)

`docs/adr/0015-actor-identity-allocation.md:168`
```
- **Session wiring.** `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts` must register
  the `identity.actor-name` stream alongside the existing three, construct
  the registry, pass it to `PrisonerOperationsRuntime`, and mint for each
  `GuardRoster.hire`. Until it does, identity is inert
```

**VERIFIED: every item is done on `main`, and the prose still says "must".** `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts`:
- `:175` — `{ name: ACTOR_IDENTITY_RNG_STREAM, state: deriveXoshiroState(masterSeed, ACTOR_IDENTITY_RNG_STREAM) },`
- `:184` — `const actorIdentity = new ActorIdentityRegistry();`
- `:186` — `const prisoners = new PrisonerOperationsRuntime({ capacity: DEFAULT_PRISONER_CAPACITY, navigation, identity: actorIdentity });`
- `:228` — `const securityGuards = new GuardRoster(DEFAULT_GUARD_CAPACITY, actorIdentity, () => rng.get(ACTOR_IDENTITY_RNG_STREAM));`

Two companion claims are also overtaken. `:102` ("the envelope field is #70's to add") and `:167` ("This ADR deliberately does not create the V3 bump") — the field shipped: `src/persistence/save-schema.ts:678` `// --- Actor identity (V3, issue #75 / ADR 0015) ---` and `:816` `identity: actorIdentitySnapshotSchema.optional(),`. And `:40` says "prisoners, staff, security, contraband and incidents are not persisted at all", while `sessionSystemsV3Schema` (`:767-775`) persists exactly `prisoners, operations, navigation, security, contraband, incidents`.

**LIVE, and it cuts both ways.** An agent reading the Consequences believes the wiring is outstanding and re-does it — double-registering a named RNG stream or constructing a second registry, either of which shifts a stream and breaks replay determinism that ADR 0009 turns into a product guarantee. An owner reading the Status believes nothing is committed, when an actor's name is already a persisted, checksummed, migration-bearing field of every V3 save — the exact thing the ADR's "What this asks a human to accept" section says must not be assumed.

**Smallest correct fix:** rewrite the wiring bullet as a statement of fact with the line numbers above; replace the "#70's to add" clauses with the shipped field; correct the "not persisted at all" sentence. Then either move the Status to Accepted (with 0012, which it extends) or add one line under the Status recording that the decision is implemented and in the save format ahead of approval — so the queue the owner reads is honest about what is already irreversible.

---

## 4. ADR 0016 asks permission for a mechanism that is already switched on and has already fired (Proposed)

`docs/adr/0016-migration-delivery-mechanism.md:5`
```
**Proposed — pending human approval.** Not accepted.
```

Its own decision §1, `:71-72`, written in the present indicative:
```
**Deploy to production** enabled, pointed at the `lockstate` project.
Merging to `main` applies migrations to it without further approval.
```

`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` carries it as a live table row — *"Migrations → Supabase **staging** | automatically, on every merge to `main`, through Supabase's own GitHub integration | none"* — and records the 71-second window on 2026-08-23 in which nine migrations went from unapplied to applied around a merge, while stating that ADR 0016 "is **Proposed, not accepted**, so it records the open decision rather than sanctioning what the table above describes."

So `main` simultaneously asserts that an irreversible, ungated, merge-triggered database mechanism is running, and that nobody has approved it. The safeguard is the ADR's own line: "Recorded as a constraint precisely because nothing enforces it mechanically." A constraint whose only enforcement is a sentence in an unapproved document is not enforcement.

**LIVE, and the only Proposed ADR whose subject can destroy data** — `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`'s Rollback section states migration rollback is not automated.

**This one needs the owner, not an edit.** ADR 0016 should be moved to Accepted, or Rejected and the integration disconnected. Until then, add under the Status: *the mechanism in §1 is nevertheless live, it applied nine migrations on 2026-08-23, so this ADR asks for retroactive approval of a running mechanism rather than permission to start one, and §2's production constraint is currently unenforced by anything but this sentence.*

(For completeness: the ADR's two Consequences to-dos are discharged — `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` was updated and `docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md` amended — which leaves the Status as the only remaining inconsistency.)

---

## The Proposed queue, which is what the owner actually needs

`docs/adr/README.md` is now the index, and `tests/foundation/adr-numbering-contract.test.ts` keeps it honest — so this table is a prioritisation, not a substitute for it. All **six**, in the order I would put them:

| ADR | Subject | State of implementation | Why it is where it is in this order |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **0016** | Which mechanism applies migrations, and to which project | Mechanism **live**; applied nine migrations to a hosted project | The only one whose subject destroys data, and rollback is not automated |
| **0013** | Free-tier cloud-save capacity | Enforced in SQL (`supabase/migrations/20260823100000_bound_free_tier_capacity.sql`); 20-revision retention and 256 MiB per account genuinely absent | Three numbers the owner must set before anyone pays for anything |
| **0021** | HTTP response security headers for the static-asset deployment | Authored `Proposed — pending human approval` | Newest entrant to this queue; not in the original five |
| **0012** | Reproducibility of derived identifiers | Taxonomy in use; table wrong (above); `GlobalTopologyId` case is #112 | ADR 0015 depends on it, so approving 0015 first approves this implicitly |
| **0015** | Actor identity is allocated, not derived | Shipped end to end, including a persisted `identity` field | Approval is retroactive; a name is already in the save format |
| **0014** | Art storage and runtime asset delivery | Implemented (`.gitattributes`, `public/_headers`, the CI `assets` job) | Decisions already made by implementation, plus one deliberately open question about publishing `public/game-content/source-art/` |

## The test that should have caught all of this

When this was filed, no test read `docs/adr/`. **That part is now built**, and it took the shape this issue proposed: `tests/foundation/adr-numbering-contract.test.ts` requires every ADR to have a parseable Status from a closed keyword set, normalises the two Status syntaxes so a machine-readable queue is possible at all, checks filename/heading agreement and unique numbering, and checks the README index against the documents in both directions.

The third bullet of the original proposal is **not** built and is still worth having: an allow-list test asserting that no `Proposed` ADR is cited from `src/**` as settled architecture (the citation shape `ADR 00NN` in a source comment is the signal). That is the one that would have caught defects 3 and 4 rather than the bookkeeping around them.

**Concrete surviving mutations at filing time:** change any Accepted ADR's Status to `Rejected`, or delete a Status block entirely — nothing noticed. The numbering contract closes that one. The deeper defects are still unguarded: removing the `'ready'` member from `WorkerState` changes no test outcome, and deleting the `pathRequestId` field from `carryItemJobSchema` fails only if a test happens to round-trip a travelling job.

Related: #117 (duplicate ADR number 0004 and the missing index — the index now exists), #260.
